# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I can feel the bomb. The strip is engraved with three marks: the first two are identical, the third is different. I cannot read them, only feel their shape. Do you have anything in the manual about a three-mark engraved strip, or what an engraved strip means? Also tell me what you can read from your manual about keypad codes and wire cutting.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. Full visual readout: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is green. STRIP is painted red, blue, yellow in that order. KEYPAD buttons: 1=2, 2=3, 3=7, 4=1, needs a 2-digit code, nothing entered. WIRES numbered: 1=orange, 2=yellow, 3=blue, 4=red, 5=white, 6=green. Blind gestured to me: two, fist, two. I cannot hear, so tell me what the manual says.

I hold the manual. The rule is exact and ordered: cut yellow, press key wearing 2, cut orange, press key wearing 7.

Deaf's readout gives me wire positions: wire 2 = yellow, wire 1 = orange. So the cuts are wire 2 then wire 1.

The keypad: buttons are 1→2, 2→3, 3→7, 4→1. "The key that wears 2" means the button whose label is 2 — that's button 1. "The key that wears 7" means the button whose label is 7 — that's button 3. So press button 1, then button 3.

But Blind is the one who can touch. Blind cannot see colors or printed labels. Blind can feel shapes. So I must translate everything into feelable positions: which wire by number/position, which key by position. Blind needs to know: cut the second wire, press the first key, cut the first wire, press the third key — assuming wires and keys are felt in numbered order left to right.

Blind also reported an engraved strip with three marks, first two identical, third different. Deaf reported the strip is painted red, blue, yellow. These may be unrelated to the defusal sequence — the manual says nothing about a strip. I should not invent meaning. I'll tell Blind the manual gives no instruction about the engraved strip; ignore it. The action is purely wires and keys.

I cannot speak. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can then relay? No — Deaf cannot speak either? Actually Deaf can hear nothing but can speak? The table: Deaf can see, cannot hear or touch. Speech is a voice. Deaf is not mute, so Deaf can speak. But turns go Mute, Blind, Deaf — I come first, then Blind, then Deaf. My gestures reach Deaf this round. Blind's message reached me. I need to get instructions to Blind, who acts. But I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf speaks and Blind hears. So I must gesture the full instruction to Deaf, who will voice it to Blind.

I need to encode positions in gestures. I'll gesture numbers as counts? Gestures are symbols only. I can gesture a sequence of symbols and Deaf will see them; Deaf can interpret if we agree. But no prior agreement. I should gesture something Deaf can read as numbers. I'll use repeated symbols: e.g., ✊ repeated n times = number n. Let me define by making it obvious: I'll gesture the wire/key sequence as pairs.

Let me just gesture a clear sequence: two ✊ (wire 2), then one ☝ (key 1), then one ✊ (wire 1), then three ✊ (key 3). Deaf sees symbols and can count. But Deaf doesn't know my encoding. I should also send words? I cannot speak. Only gestures.

Hmm, this is the core difficulty. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf must interpret. I'll make the gesture sequence as self-evident as possible and hope Deaf reasons: the manual order is yellow, key-2, orange, key-7. Deaf knows wire2=yellow, wire1=orange, key wearing 2 = button1, key wearing 7 = button3. So Deaf can derive it themselves if I just confirm the manual. But I can't speak to confirm.

I can gesture the manual's structure: I'll gesture four items in order. Use ✊ to mean "wire" and ☝ to mean "key"? Then ✊✊ = wire 2, ☝ = key... but which key? I need the number.

Alternative: gesture the actual numbers as repeated symbols with separators. Let me gesture: ✊ ✊ (2) ✋ (separator) ☝ (1) ✋ ✊ (1) ✋ ☝☝☝ (3). Deaf counts runs. Risky but best available.

Actually simpler: I can gesture the four actions as: [2 wires worth] [1 key] [1 wire] [3 key]. I'll gesture ✊✊ then ☝ then ✊ then ☝☝☝. Deaf sees 2 fists, 1 point, 1 fist, 3 points. If Deaf maps fist=wire-count and point=key-count, and knows manual order yellow/key2/orange/key7, Deaf can match: yellow=wire2 (two fists ✓), key wearing 2 = button1 (one point ✓), orange=wire1 (one fist ✓), key wearing 7 = button3 (three points ✓). That's a consistent decode. Good.

I'll also gesture to Deaf that the strip is irrelevant — maybe a dismissive gesture. I'll include 👎 for the strip.

Let me send one gesture message to Deaf with the sequence, and also address Blind? I cannot reach Blind directly — gestures only reach Deaf. So only Deaf.

I'll write the calls.I hold the manual, and the manual is unambiguous: cut the yellow wire, press the key wearing 2, cut the orange wire, press the key wearing 7 — in that order only.

From Deaf's readout I can resolve everything into positions:
- Yellow wire = wire 2
- Orange wire = wire 1
- Key wearing 2 = the button labeled 2 = button 1
- Key wearing 7 = the button labeled 7 = button 3

So the action sequence is: cut wire 2, press key 1, cut wire 1, press key 3.

Blind is the only one who can act, and Blind cannot see colors or printed labels — only feel positions. So the instructions must arrive as positions, not colors. But I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, so Deaf must relay to Blind.

I'll gesture the sequence as counts so Deaf can decode: fists = wire number, points = key number, in the manual's order. Two fists (wire 2), one point (key 1), one fist (wire 1), three points (key 3). Deaf knows wire2=yellow, wire1=orange, key-wearing-2=button1, key-wearing-7=button3, so this decode is forced and consistent.

Blind's engraved strip: the manual says nothing about any strip, so it is not part of the defusal. I'll gesture a dismissive mark for it so Deaf doesn't chase it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✊","☝","✊","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

I hold the manual. It is fixed and simple: cut yellow, press key wearing 2, cut orange, press key wearing 7 — in that order only. Deaf misread my gestures as binary. That was not my intent, but it doesn't matter: I should not rely on Deaf decoding an encoding I invented. The cleaner path is to give Deaf the *positions* directly, since Deaf already knows the mapping and can voice it to Blind in plain numbers.

The resolution:
- Yellow wire = wire 2.
- Orange wire = wire 1.
- Key wearing 2 = the button labeled 2 = button 1.
- Key wearing 7 = the button labeled 7 = button 3.

So: cut wire 2, press key 1, cut wire 1, press key 3.

Deaf asked me to spell it out in gestures. I'll gesture it unambiguously by using a separator and repeating a single symbol a countable number of times, and I'll make the *order* explicit as four groups. But Deaf already has the mapping, so the most robust thing is to gesture the four numbers in sequence with clear separators: 2, 1, 1, 3. Use ✊ as the counting symbol and ✋ as separator between numbers. That gives Deaf four runs: two fists, one fist, one fist, three fists → 2,1,1,3.

I cannot reach Blind directly; only Deaf. So Deaf must relay to Blind. I'll also gesture that the strip is irrelevant (👎) and that there is no keypad code (👎).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✊","✋","✊","✋","✊","✋","✊","✊","✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👎"])
```

then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. UPDATE: DISPLAY back to 6, LIGHT now yellow. KEYPAD 1=2 2=3 3=7 4=1, needs 2 digits, nothing entered. WIRES 1=orange 2=yellow 3=blue 4=red 5=white 6=green. Better: I can gesture a message that is *self-describing by count of a single repeated symbol with separators*, and explicitly tell Deaf via the count that there are four numbers. But Deaf will still guess.

The cleanest available channel: I cannot speak, Blind cannot see. Deaf can both see my gestures and speak to Blind. The bottleneck is Deaf's misreading. I'll gesture the resolved sequence as four groups separated by ✋, each group being ✊ repeated the right number of times: 2, 1, 1, 3. I'll keep it minimal and repeat it identically so Deaf sees the same four groups twice and stops guessing binary.

Also Blind's gesture "point-up, fist, open-hand-five" — Blind says it means position1, same-as-first, different, describing the engraving. Not relevant to defusal.

I'll send the four groups again, clearly, and a confirmation gesture. And I'll gesture to Deaf the four numbers as counts: ✊✊ / ✊ / ✊ / ✊✊✊.

